Subject: Reranker integration + evaluation questions — next steps

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have a shared plan for the reranker eval/integration: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- You want to improve search relevance across product pages and customer Q&A using an embeddings + reranker pipeline.
- Primary metrics: NDCG@10 and precision@3 for product search queries; offline A/B on conversion later.
- Target latency for reranker inference: 60–100ms p95 (we discussed async batch options).

Proposed technical approach
1) Use Redwood embeddings for candidate retrieval (faiss) + Redwood Reranker API for re-ranking top_k results.
2) Offline eval: we’ll run the reranker over your labeled testset (please see attached sample: reranker_eval_dataset.csv) and return NDCG/P@k breakdowns for top_k in [5,10,20].
3) Online integration options: a) synchronous rerank (low top_k, optimized kernels) b) async rerank with progressive results streaming (recommended if top_k >= 20).

Action items
- Oliver/Priya: share a 1k-5k labeled sample (CSV or JSONL) with ID/query/doc pairs and relevance labels. We received the small sample you shared in the call; could you confirm format and send the larger set?
- Dev: run a quick baseline on our side using the sample we have and share preliminary metrics + hyperparams (scoring, top_k).
- Marissa: coordinate contracting and timeline, share proposal and next meeting invite.

Attachments: reranker_eval_dataset.csv (sample), proposal_ACME_v3.pdf (commercial).

Tentative timeline
- Baseline run (Dev): 3 business days after we receive the 1k sample
- Evaluation report: 5–7 business days after baseline

I’ll set up a short follow-up next week — please confirm preferred times.

Hi Oliver — nice questions. Quick answers and a suggested evaluation plan: 

1) Input format: text-snippets (title + description + specs) are sufficient for initial reranker evaluation and will keep the evaluation fast. If you have structured fields (brand, category), include them as separate columns — we can concatenate but also pass as metadata for feature-crossing. Raw HTML is fine but expect preprocessing time; recommend keeping offline eval to text-snippets first.

2) Labels: graded relevance (0/1/2) is preferred — it gives us more signal for NDCG computations. If you only have binary today, we can still run evaluation (P@k) but NDCG will be weaker.

3) top_k tuning: start with reranking top_k = [5, 10, 20]. Our pattern is:
   - top_k=5: minimal latency, good for very-latency-sensitive pages
   - top_k=10: balance of latency and quality (good default)
   - top_k=20: better recall for long-tail but higher cost/latency; consider async streaming for top_k>=20.

Evaluation plan (what I’ll run once you send the 2k sample)
- Baseline (embeddings retrieval only): compute recall@k and P@k for candidate set
- Reranker (Redwood Reranker API): compute NDCG@5/10/20, P@3, and delta vs baseline
- Hyperparams to sweep: top_k [5,10,20], scorer temperature / fusion weights if we use ensemble signals
- Perf targets: we’ll measure per-request p50/p95 latency on a test harness that approximates your QPS.

Notes on integration APIs
- Ranking API: POST /v1/rerank with body {"query", "candidates": [...], "top_k": N}. Returns scored list and token-level debug if enabled.
- Embeddings: we recommend batching candidate embeddings and caching vector store; we can provide an SDK sample for Python/Node.

I attached a quick script stub and the small eval sample we used (reranker_eval_dataset.csv). I’ll run the baseline Monday and share initial numbers.

Attachments: reranker_eval_dataset.csv (attached - sample), reranker_eval_script.py (inline snippet)
